newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares slip on prospect of changes in budget.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares slip on prospect of changes in budget.

text.p: Delhi share prices opened lower in nervous trade on Monday amid prospects the leftwing parties in the ruling United Front coalition might force some changes in the proposed 1997/98 (April-March) budget, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index was 4.21 points lower at 786.33 points after 30 minutes of trade.

India's two communist parties are seeking to roll back proposed cuts in tax rates and import tariffs. Parliament begins debate on the Finance Bill, which incorporates tax and tariff proposals, on Wednesday.

"Fears that Finance Minister Chidambaram might be forced to make changes in the budgetary proposals before getting it passed in the parliament triggered selling," said Yogesh Sethi of Vinayaka Investments.
Reliance Industries fell 3.50 rupees to 301.00 on speculative selling, brokers said.
State Bank of India fell 4.95 rupees to 308.00.
